references.text: The preceding verse lists the other ingredients in the holy anointing oil: myrrh, cinnamon, and calamus
The next verse describes how these ingredients are to be blended into a holy anointing oil
A hin of olive oil is also mentioned in connection with offerings and holy purposes
The sanctuary shekel is used as the standard unit of measure for holy purposes
The sanctuary shekel as the standard weight unit in tabernacle service
The sanctuary shekel defined as twenty gerahs, the standardized weight unit
Pure olive oil used for the lamp in the tabernacle, showing the holy use of olive oil
Pure, pressed olive oil required for tabernacle service
Cassia (קִדָּה) mentioned among Solomon's spice imports, the same ingredient
The anointing oil used at the consecration of Aaron and his sons
Highlights the transition from God's instructions regarding holy measures in Exodus to their concrete application through the offerings of the tribes in Numbers.
Illustrates how the fixed weight established in Exodus was consistently observed by each individual tribe in the consecration ritual.
Confirms the universal validity of the sanctuary's weight standards as set forth in Exodus for all the tribes of Israel.
Shows the repeated obedience to God's specific requirements regarding weights and materials in the consecration ritual.
Demonstrates that the standard for holy measures established in Exodus was the foundation for all offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle.
Emphasizes the consequence of following God's specific weight standards for holy objects throughout the consecration process.
Highlights how divine authority over weights and measures from Exodus was enforced in each tribe's offering.
Marks the first practical example of using the sanctuary's weight standards as established in Exodus.
Supports the theme of unified obedience to God's specific requirements for weights and materials.
Confirms that the standard for holy measurements applied to all tribes without exception.
